historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management guidance (FY2027 revenue $825-840m vs FY2026 underlying $826.1m is approximately flat), not a historical CAGR -- the FY2018-2020 equity and FCF series are distorted by two goodwill/programming impairments and the 10:1 2021-22 share consolidation, so mechanical CAGRs do not describe the current business.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity and FCF 5yr CAGRs are deeply negative (impairment-driven, FY2018-2019) while revenue is roughly flat; the divergence is a legacy-impairment artefact, not a signal about current earnings power. Base-case growth instead anchors on FY2027 guidance and management's own FY31 ambition, tapering toward the structural satellite-decline rate by year 5-10.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 lands inside guidance (revenue $825-840m, EBITDA $155-165m) and Sky Free synergies reach the promised $10m+ by FY28, holding revenue roughly flat for three years and lifting the EBITDA margin from 19.0% to about 20.5%. From FY2030 the arithmetic of the core reasserts itself: Sky Box is ~54% of revenue and shrinking 5-8% a year, and streaming, advertising and broadband are too small to offset it, so group revenue drifts to -1.5%/yr and the margin eases back as the mix shifts toward lower-margin advertising and free-to-air. The cheaper NZR deal (~$75-80m/yr vs ~$111m) and the renewed NRL/Premier League rights (management frames both as supportive of continued programming-cost discipline within the 47-49% target) are genuine and durable margin support, and capex normalises to the guided 6-8% of revenue now the Optus satellite migration is finished.
scenario_narratives.bull: Sky Free is the pivot management says it is: advertising and BVOD scale on the acquired Three/ThreeNow inventory, digital advertising compounds off its small base, broadband keeps growing ~15%, and together they genuinely offset satellite attrition so group revenue grows ~1.5-2%/yr toward the stated FY2031 ambition of 20-30% of revenue from non-subscription sources. Synergies exceed $10m, programming costs settle at the 47% end of the 47-49% target aided by the renewed rights economics, and the EBITDA margin reaches 23% - above the 21-23% three-year target Sky only just delivered. Capex falls to the bottom of the 6-8% envelope. Even here the exit is capped at 5.6x EV/EBITDA, the highest multiple this market has paid in a decade.
scenario_narratives.bear: The satellite base decays faster than 5-8% as households cut discretionary spend in a weak NZ economy, and Neon's rebound stalls against a standalone HBO Max that launched in NZ on 16 June 2026 after Sky chose not to renew exclusivity. The acquired free-to-air business is a declining linear-advertising asset in a contracting market, and integration synergies are consumed by content inflation rather than dropping to EBITDA. The new seven-year NRL commitment (~NZ$61m/yr from 2028, subject to shareholder approval) is a large fixed obligation locked in before the FY31 strategic plan is even finalised, and if audience/ad-revenue support doesn't materialise it becomes a margin drag rather than a synergy. Because the satellite cost base is largely fixed - transponder, field technicians, set-top hardware - a shrinking subscriber base produces operating deleverage, so the margin falls from 19% to 13.5%. The 2030 NZR renewal reprices against Sky again, or fragments further to a global streamer. Revenue declines ~4.5%/yr and terminal growth is negative.

valuation_philosophy.summary: This is an income stock, not a growth stock, and should be valued as one. Reported FY2026 numbers are flattered by a one-off $31.4m bargain-purchase gain and $8.2m of Optus compensation; this model uses Sky's own underlying revenue/EBITDA, normalised free cash flow, and a normal 28% NZ tax rate throughout. The core Sky Box satellite base has fallen ~5-8%/yr for several years and is the majority of revenue; FY2026's headline growth was acquisition-driven (Discovery NZ/Sky Free), not organic, and FY2027 guidance at the midpoint is essentially flat. The investment case rests on the ~9% fully-imputed dividend yield and a net-cash balance sheet (no bank debt since FY2023), not on compounding. The FY2026 dividend of 32cps costs more than underlying earnings (~105% of underlying EPS) but is comfortably covered by normalised free cash flow (74.9%, within the newly formalised 60-90% payout policy), and the FY2027 guidance of at least 35cps sits near the top of that band against this model's year-1 owner FCF.
key_risks_to_valuation: Structural satellite subscriber decline (Sky Box, ~54% of revenue) continuing at or faster than the historical 5-8%/yr rate
Neon and the broader streaming push failing to offset satellite decline against a newly-launched standalone HBO Max competitor

The new ~NZ$61m/yr, seven-year NRL rights commitment (2028-2034, pending shareholder approval) becoming a fixed-cost burden if audience/advertising support does not materialise as the linear-TV ad market remains contracted
Dividend policy (60-90% of normalised FCF, 10%/yr growth target FY27-29) coming under pressure if capex exceeds the guided 6-8% of revenue envelope or FCF normalisation assumptions prove optimistic
Sky Free integration synergies (target at least $10m EBITDA by FY28) failing to drop through to margin, being consumed instead by content cost inflation

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 share-based payment $0.396m (FY2026 not separately disclosed; immaterial). NZX-typical near-zero SBC.
inputs.price_as_of: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close, 2026-09-25T05:00:32Z; 52-week range 3.05-3.90
inputs.wacc_rationale: 13% WACC in all scenarios, NZD-matched: small-cap NZX illiquidity premium plus single-country/regulatory concentration loaded into the discount rate; structural subscriber-decline and sports-rights renewal risk are instead charged once, inside the scenario FLOWS (growth and margin paths), per the owner-fcf-adaptations single-risk-charge rule.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B: lease principal repaid deducted inside the flows via lease_cost_pct (~3.0-3.3% of revenue); the $62.5m of lease liabilities (100% of total_debt -- Sky has had zero bank borrowings since FY2023) is excluded from net_debt to avoid double-counting.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest immaterial ($0.423m of FY26 profit, 0.7% of NPAT; $1.708m of equity). Not modelled separately.
inputs.notes: UPDATE, not a fresh build. MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md -- Sky is an operating company (media/broadcasting), so the owner-FCF engine plus the non-US adaptations (references/owner-fcf-adaptations.md) applies: (a) NZD-matched WACC; (b) lease Treatment B; (c) NCI immaterial, charged once; (d) interest income stripped because net cash sits in the bridge; (e) SBC-zero market, band_position null; (f) risk charged once -- structural decline and rights risk in the flows, only illiquidity/single-country premium in WACC. Owner FCF uses Sky's own normalised free cash flow ($58.9m -- OCF less lease principal less capex, excluding one-offs, tax-normalised to 28%) less interest income $1.753m = $57.15m; see fcf_bridge for the full walk from reported FCF $89.3m. Revenue base is FY2026 UNDERLYING revenue $826.1m (not reported $824.8m), because reported NPAT of $59.8m contains a non-recurring $31.4m bargain-purchase gain (Discovery NZ acquired for $1) and $8.2m of Optus satellite-migration compensation, partly offset by $13.9m of Sky Free integration costs. THIS REFRESH: prior DCF (2026-08-28) was already built on FY2026 final annual results -- the FY2026 Metrics.csv change this cycle was an EPS unit rescale only (cents to whole NZD; the underlying revenue/EBITDA/NPAT/cash/shares figures are unchanged), and the qualitative refresh added the NRL broadcast rights renewal (~NZ$61m/yr, 2028-2034, shareholder approval pending), Premier League extension to 2034, and Olympic rights to 2032. These are confirmed as RENEWALS of existing rights relationships Sky already carries (NRL rights are not new to the portfolio), management explicitly frames the new NZR/NRL/Premier League economics as supportive of continued programming-cost discipline (47-49% of revenue target, delivered at 47.3% in FY26, reaffirmed for FY27), and no new cost figure contradicts the margin paths already in this model. DRIVER PATHS THEREFORE HELD UNCHANGED from the 2026-08-28 build -- growth, margin, SBC%, capex%, lease-cost%, tax and WACC paths are identical in every scenario. Only the price anchor (3.49 -> 3.50) and price_as_of are refreshed. Evidence that would move a driver: the NRL deal's actual annual cost disclosed at shareholder-approval EGM (expected within FY27), or a break from the 47-49% programming-cost target in FY27 actuals.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 9.03x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear held at 30% (above the 15% house default) because the central risk is structural, not cyclical: the majority of revenue sits in a satellite base that has declined every reporting period for five years, and the designated replacement growth engine (Neon) only just stabilised against a new standalone HBO Max competitor. The new seven-year NRL commitment (~NZ$61m/yr, pending shareholder approval) adds a large fixed cost obligation into this bear case. Bull held at 20% because it requires several independent things to go right at once - synergies exceeding target, an advertising turnaround in a market that only recently stopped contracting, AND a margin above a 21-23% target Sky has only just delivered for the first time. Base holds 50%: FY2027 guidance is credible, near-term visibility is good, and the sports-rights renewals (NZR, NRL, Premier League, Olympics) all through 2030-2034 give unusually long revenue-cost visibility for a media business.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
